title: fix(history): mark list and depth truncation on the wire
body:
Paired: [GitHub #10852](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/pull/10852) ↔ [GitCode !9723](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/merge_requests/9723)

/kind bug

## What changed

- `_sanitize_history_wire_value` now reports what it cuts: the owning mapping gains a `<key>_truncated: true` sibling and the record gains `truncated: true`.
- Lists are still trimmed to 100 items and depth is still capped at 8, but the result is now detectable from the payload.
- A pre-set falsy flag (for example `global_file_ops_truncated: false` shipped in a tool payload) is upgraded to `true`; a pre-set truthy one (the live path's `raw_output_truncated`) is kept as is.
- The MCP App block is excluded from the stats and restored byte-for-byte, so a block the client receives in full carries no marker and cannot push a near-budget record into the collapse path. When the marked record overflows the 64 KiB budget, the unmarked form is measured once more and served if it fits.

## Why

String truncation already describes itself with a visible " [truncated]" suffix; list and depth cuts did not. On reopen or history paging the client therefore received structured tool data that no longer matched `history.jsonl`, with nothing in the payload saying it had been cut.

Fixes #6269

## Self-checklist

- [x] Design: additive wire change; no existing field changes type or value, and no UI work is needed for the markers to be correct
- [x] Tests: `tests/unit_tests/agentserver/test_history_wire_truncation_markers.py` (12 cases) plus the MCP App fidelity case extended
- [x] Validation: see below
- [x] Interface: no public interface change
- [x] Docs: no user-facing documentation change

## Validation

- `pytest tests/unit_tests/agentserver/test_history_payload_limits.py tests/unit_tests/agentserver/test_split_history_record_for_stream.py tests/unit_tests/agentserver/test_history_get_stream_split.py tests/unit_tests/test_mcp_apps.py` → 29 passed, 6 skipped, identical to the run before the change
- New and related history/wire suites together: 90 passed, 6 skipped
- Manual: a 150-item list stays an array, keeps 100 items and carries `items_truncated` / `raw_output_truncated` / `truncated`; the record is 1479 bytes on the wire
- Manual: the MCP App fidelity record produces no marker of any kind
- Manual: a record that fits only without markers is served unmarked instead of collapsing (blob 65066..65139 band)

## Compatibility

Additive only: unknown sibling keys are ignored by current readers, the per-record 64 KiB budget still bounds the frame, and an oversized record still collapses. In the narrow band where the markers alone would overflow the budget, the record is served unmarked — its data is intact and its behaviour matches the previous version.
